artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S$ denote the class of functions $f(z) = z + a_2 z^2 + a_3 z^3 + \cdots$ that are analytic and univalent in the open unit disk $U = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z| < 1\}$, normalized by $f(0) = 0$ and $f'(0) = 1$. Endow $S$ with the topology of uniform convergence on compact subsets of $U$ (equivalently, the topology induced by the locally convex space $H(U)$ of all functions analytic on $U$). Then $S$ is a compact subset of $H(U)$.

A function $f \in S$ is called an \emph{extreme point} of $S$ if $f$ cannot be written as $f = 	frac{1}{2}(g + h)$ with $g, h \in S$ and $g 
e h$ (i.e., $f$ is an extreme point of the convex hull of $S$ that lies in $S$).

A function $f \in S$ is called a \emph{support point} of $S$ if there exists a continuous complex-valued linear functional $L$ on $H(U)$, not constant on $S$, such that
$$\operatorname{Re} L(f) = \max_{g \in S} \operatorname{Re} L(g).$$

Answer the following two questions:

(a) Is every extreme point of $S$ a support point of $S$?

(b) Is every support point of $S$ an extreme point of $S$?
artifact.status_search_result: The two questions of P. L. Duren on whether every extreme point of $S$ is a support point and conversely are classical problems in geometric function theory. While much is known about support points (e.g., they are single-slit mappings with analytic omitted arcs) and about extreme points (e.g., they have monotonic modulus and omit unbounded sets), the literature still treats both implications as unresolved. Recent works (e.g., on generalized support points and extensions to several complex variables) continue to study these notions without claiming a resolution to Duren's questions, suggesting they remain open.

status_evidence.title: Extreme Points and Support Points - ScienceDirect (Handbook of Complex Analysis)
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys properties of extreme and support points of S; notes both classes of points share monotonic modulus property but the precise relationship is not fully resolved.
status_evidence.claim: The relationship between extreme points and support points of S is treated as a continuing area of investigation.

status_evidence.title: Generalized support points of the set of univalent functions
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs an extreme point of S whose omitted set is not an analytic arc, hence not a support point in the usual sense, by considering generalized support points.
status_evidence.claim: Indicates work toward, but not full resolution of, Duren's questions about extreme vs. support points.
